items.title: The actual first-column law

source.label: Zhou–Suzuki, B.7: actual first-column transport before Lemma A.1
source.anchor: Appendix B.2.2 Proposition B.7 proof, Eq21–24, sentence that O e_1 is uniform on the unit sphere; bounded first-column transport component only, before Lemma A.1 evaluation
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. A bounded source-implicit component of the statement that the first orthogonal column is uniformly spherical, together with transport of the unevaluated selected Gaussian normalization. Identification with canonical normalized surface measure and both Poisson values remain separate.
source.scope: Probability, unit-sphere support, full orthogonal invariance of the actual first-column law and transport of the existing actual signed Gaussian expectation to an absolutely integrable ambient first-column kernel. Canonical normalized surface measure identification/uniqueness and Poisson evaluations remain OPEN; no Eq24 value, positive TV ratio, query/cost, hidden-eigenbasis or main theorem.

items.statement:
For natural \(n\ge3\) and real \(\kappa\ge4\), set \(s=\sqrt\kappa\), \(r=(1-1/n)(s-1)/(s+1)\), \(\ell=(4ns+(s-1)^2)/(8n(n-1))\), and \( eta=(-1)^{n-1}(s-1)^{n-1}(1-1/n)^{n/2}/(s+1)^n\). Let \(\mu\) be normalized Haar probability on full \(O(n)\), \(c(O)=Oe_1\) in genuine Euclidean space and \(
u=c_*\mu\). Put \(f(y)=((s+1)y_1-(s-1))/(1+r^2-2ry_1)^{n/2}\), using real half-dimension powers. Let \(A_O=((\kappa+1)/2)I-((\kappa-1)/4)(O+O^	op)\), \(\gamma_O=\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1})\), and \(H_\gamma(\ell)=\mathbb E_\mu[\det(O)\int e^{-\ell\|x\|_2^2}\,d\gamma_O]\). Then \(
u\) is a probability, \(\|y\|_2=1\) almost surely, \(Q_*
u=
u\) for every fixed full orthogonal matrix \(Q\), \(f\in L^1(
u)\), and \(H_\gamma(\ell)= eta\int f\,d
u\). This does not yet identify \(
u\) with canonical normalized surface measure or give either Poisson integral value.
assumptions: Exactly \(n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), including \(\kappa=4\). All parameter divisions are real, and \(n/2\) is a real exponent even for odd dimensions.
\(\mu\) is the existing actual normalized Haar probability on full \(O(n)\), including reflections. \(c(O)=Oe_1\) uses the Euclidean l2 norm, and \(\nu=c_*\mu\) is its literal ambient pushforward.

Probability, unit-sphere support, invariance and absolute L1 are proved conclusions. The quotient need not be continuous or have positive denominator off the support; global Borel measurability suffices for transport. No sphere law or Poisson identity is a caller premise.
